page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is a compute-aligned virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the x86_64 architecture with clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The instance supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It features 96 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation, alongside 260 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. Local ephemeral storage is bundled via a 2,835 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware is present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top 25 percent across multiple compute and throughput domains. It produces a PassMark CPU score of 63,378.89 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,188.0, with image processing scoring in the top 10 percent. Memory bandwidth remains high, reaching 255.6 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 104.85 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the server handled 67.02 million Redis SET operations per second, achieved 81.17 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and posted strong results in software compilation with Clang.

Given the 2.0 GB per vCPU memory density, this configuration is oriented toward compute-heavy rather than memory-heavy environments. The integration of 2.8 TB of fast local NVMe storage reduces reliance on external network volumes for temporary files and disk scratch space. This profile is well matched for software compilation, CI/CD runners, containerized web clusters, caching tiers, and localized database operations requiring sustained CPU frequency and high local IOPS.
description: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is a compute-focused instance powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor across 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 96 GB of RAM, the system delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation and includes 2,835 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, with no graphics hardware included. Architectural features include 260 MB of L3 cache along with Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-quartile ratings in PassMark CPU performance (63,378.89), Geekbench Clang compilation (45,145.0), and image processing. Memory and I/O subsystems sustain high throughput, achieving 67.02 million Redis SET operations per second and 81.17 GB/sec web serving transfer rates. The instance operates efficiently for compute-bound tasks requiring rapid local scratch storage, such as CI/CD build farms, web services, and caching workloads.
